init.title: Configuring this gateway
init.description:
**Gateway**: {gateway}

This is where the gateway is configured and where “basic” covers are calibrated - the ones whose position Home Assistant has to estimate from their run times.

Profiles and covers can also be managed from the [panel](/myhome-calibration).

**What you have to do**: choose an option. Nothing is written until something is saved, what is saved is applied when this dialog is closed, and no cover moves before a screen says it is about to.

gateway.title: Gateway and connection
gateway.description: Where the gateway is, how it is spoken to, and where the configuration file lives. Saving reloads the integration with the new values.

data.generate_events: Generate events in Home Assistant for each message received

data_description.command_worker_count: How many command sessions the integration opens to the gateway. More sessions send queued commands in parallel, but gateways hold only a handful. Default 1 (1-4).
data_description.idle_watchdog_sec: No frame received on the monitor session for this long: a harmless probe is sent through the command session. Default 300 s (60-3600).
data_description.probe_window_sec: How long the probe is given to be answered. If nothing arrives on the monitor session and the gateway acknowledges no status request on the command session within this time, the connection is rebuilt. Default 30 s (5-300).
data_description.command_timeout_sec: How long a single command may take to be written and acknowledged before it is retried once and then dropped. Default 10 s (2-60).
data_description.queue_ttl_sec: Commands still queued after this long are dropped instead of being sent late. Default 60 s (10-600).
data_description.default_keepalive_minutes: Keep-alive requested from the energy meters when keepalive_minutes is set neither on the sensor nor in the gateway's sensor_defaults: block (alias energy:) of the configuration file. 0 disables it. Default 125 min (0-255).

profiles_covers.title: Profiles and covers
profiles_covers.description:
A **profile** describes one kind of cover: how long it takes to run, how long the slats take to open and how the curtain winds onto the roller. Every cover may follow one, and Home Assistant scales it to that cover's own curtain travel.

Profiles: {profiles} · Basic covers: {covers}

menu_options.pick_profile: View, edit or delete a profile

assign_covers.title: Which profile each cover follows
assign_covers.description:
**What is about to happen**: nothing moves. Assigning a profile means telling Home Assistant “this cover is built like those ones”: from then on the cover follows that profile, including its run times, scaled to this cover's curtain travel.

The profile is assigned here after the configuration file was written, so it takes precedence over the file's values for this cover, if you use one. Values measured on this cover still take precedence wherever they are available. Later changes to the profile apply to every cover that follows it.

A `profile:` written in the configuration file for a cover is shown here as its current value and cannot be taken away from this screen: it is defined in the file and must be managed there.

**Where each cover's values come from today**: {covers}.

**What you have to do**: pick a profile for each cover, or “No profile” to leave it on the file's values or the defaults.

assign_heights.title: What is the curtain travel of these covers?
assign_heights.description:
A profile contains measurements from a cover of a given curtain travel and is scaled to other covers in proportion to their own. The following covers have no known curtain travel, so the profile cannot be scaled to them: {covers}.

**What you have to do**: measure, for each of them, the distance the bottom edge travels from fully closed to fully open, and write it in centimetres. Decimals may be written with a comma or with a point.

pick_profile.title: Which profile?
pick_profile.description: **What you have to do**: pick the profile whose values you want to see or change. The next screen also lists the covers that follow it.

profile_actions.title: Cover profile
profile_actions.description:
**Profile**: “{profile}”

Covers following it: {count}.

**What you have to do**: choose what to do with it. Viewing the values changes nothing; editing them or deleting the profile is written at once and applied when this dialog is closed.

profile_view.title: Values of profile “{profile}”

profile_edit.title: Edit profile “{profile}”
profile_edit.description:
**What is about to happen**: the values below replace the measured ones, for every cover that follows this profile. The cover does not move: only the values are changed.

**What you have to do**: change only the values for which you have more reliable information than the calibration, such as the run times in the manufacturer's specifications. Leave the other values unchanged. Decimals may be written with a comma or with a point.

data_description.reference_height: The curtain travel of the cover this profile was measured on (20-500).
data_description.opening_time: Seconds from fully closed to fully open, slats included (1-600).
data_description.closing_time: Seconds from fully open to fully closed (1-600).
data_description.slat_time: Seconds the slats take to open before the curtain starts to rise (0-60).
data_description.opening_roll: The ratio between the diameter of the roll with the cover fully open (a full tube) and with it fully closed (an empty tube): 1.5 to 2.5 on most shutters, 1 a tube whose diameter never changes (1-5).

profile_delete.title: Delete this profile?
profile_delete.description:
**Profile**: “{profile}”

**What is about to happen**: the profile is deleted and these {count} covers go back to the values of the configuration file, if you use one, or to the defaults: {covers}

{assigned} of them were given the profile here, and {from_file} follow it through the `profile:` key of the configuration file, which this deletion does not touch.

What was measured on each cover stays where it is: only the description of the kind is removed. If a profile of the same name exists in `cover_profiles:`, it stops being shadowed: the covers whose configuration file names it follow that one again, while the covers that were given the profile here alone are left following none.

profile_deleted.title: Profile “{profile}” deleted
profile_deleted.description:
The profile is gone. Covers that followed it and went back to the file's values or to the defaults: {count} - {covers}

{assigned} of them had been given the profile here; {from_file} follow it through the `profile:` key of the configuration file, which is untouched.

A profile of the same name in `cover_profiles:` is no longer shadowed and applies again to the covers whose configuration file names it.

If the profile was deleted by mistake, run the full measurement again on a cover of this kind and give the new profile the same name.

calibrations.title: Calibrations
calibrations.description:
Covers with specific values stored by the integration: {count}. Values stored here take precedence over those in the configuration file, if you use one.

**What you have to do**: pick the cover whose values you want to see, correct or delete.

no_calibrations.title: Nothing is stored yet
no_calibrations.description:
No cover of this gateway has values of its own kept by the integration: they all run on what the configuration file says, if you use one, or on the defaults.

**What you have to do**: go back to the menu and pick “Calibrate a cover” to measure one.

no_basic_covers.title: There is nothing to calibrate
no_basic_covers.description:
Every cover of this gateway reports its own position, so Home Assistant does not have to estimate it and there is no run time to measure.

The guided calibration is only for “basic” covers, the ones whose actuator does not say where it is.

calibration_actions.title: Calibration of this cover

calibration_view.title: Values of {cover}
calibration_view.description:
This is what the integration keeps for this cover:

{values}
**Where its values come from**: {origin}.

The keys listed here take precedence over those in the configuration file, if you use one; the ones that do not appear go on coming from the file, from the profile or from the defaults.

calibration_edit.title: Edit the values of {cover}
calibration_edit.description:
**What is about to happen**: the values below apply to this cover alone and take precedence over both the profile and the configuration file. The cover does not move: only the values are changed.

**What you have to do**: enter only the values you want to set for this cover. Leaving a field empty does not mean zero: it restores the value from the profile or the file. Decimals may be written with a comma or with a point.

data_description.height: How far the bottom edge travels from fully closed to fully open (20-500).
data_description.opening_time: Seconds from fully closed to fully open, slats included (1-600).
data_description.closing_time: Seconds from fully open to fully closed (1-600).
data_description.slat_time: Seconds the slats take to open before the curtain starts to rise (0-60).
data_description.opening_roll: The ratio between the diameter of the roll with the cover fully open (a full tube) and with it fully closed (an empty tube): 1.5 to 2.5 on most shutters, 1 a tube whose diameter never changes (1-5).

calibration_delete.title: Delete this calibration?

calibration_deleted.title: Calibration deleted
calibration_deleted.description: {cover} no longer has values of its own kept by the integration: it runs on what the configuration file says, if you use one, on the profile it follows, or on the defaults.

calibrate.title: Guided cover calibration
calibrate.description:
This tool calibrates “basic” covers: the ones whose actuator does not report its position. For those, the percentage you see in Home Assistant is an estimate computed from the run times; the calibration measures those times and the geometry of the roller, so as to obtain a more accurate estimate.

It will not be perfect. Expect a few centimetres out: 1-2 cm near the end stops, 2-4 cm at intermediate positions. Every full open or close re-synchronises the estimate, so the error does not build up.

“Advanced” covers report their position by themselves and need none of this, which is why they do not appear in the list in the next steps.

**What is about to happen**: you will pick a cover and one of three ways of measuring it. The cover will run to its end stops several times.

**What you have to do**: keep a tape measure to hand, make sure nothing is in the cover's way, and stay where you can see it. Nothing is saved until the last screen: you can close this dialog whenever you like and nothing will have changed, and a run already under way ends by itself at the end stop.

cover.title: Which cover are we measuring?
cover.description:
Only the “basic” covers of this gateway are listed: the ones that do not report their own position and are therefore the only ones it makes sense to calibrate with this tool.

**Which one to pick**: if this is the first time, pick a cover that is representative of its kind and easy to measure - one you can stand in front of without moving furniture, whose bottom edge a tape measure reaches. What is measured on this one will hold for every cover like it.

**What you have to do**: go and stand in front of the cover you have chosen, with this tool to hand (your phone or your laptop), and then confirm it below. You will be asked to watch it move and to measure it with a tape, so you have to be physically next to the cover you choose.

path.title: How do you want to measure this cover?
path.description:
**Cover**: {cover}

There are three ways, and the right one depends on what you have measured already. They are not steps in a sequence: you pick one.

The first (A) is the long one, about four minutes: three button presses and three tape readings. It ends in a **profile**, the description of this kind of cover, which every similar cover (same model, same size, ...) can then reuse.

The second (B) is meant precisely for covers similar to one already calibrated: pick the profile, measure the curtain travel, done.

The third (C) is for a cover that has been given a profile but stops in the wrong place: in that case the calibration of this cover has to be corrected.

**What you have to do**: pick one of the ways below. Nothing moves until the next screen.

menu_options.path_a: (A) It is the first cover of its kind (full measurement, ~4 minutes)
menu_options.path_b: (B) It is similar to a cover already measured (curtain travel only)
menu_options.path_c: (C) It has a profile but stops in the wrong place (correction)

path_a.title: Before the cover starts moving
path_a.description:
**Cover**: {cover}

**What is about to happen**: the calibration is divided into steps. At each step the cover makes the movements that step needs. Where there is a button to press, the instructions come first and the movement waits for you to start it; the steps measured with the tape move by themselves, and a screen warns you before the first of them. Eight movements in all, about four minutes.

**What you have to do**: make sure nothing is in the way - an open casement, plants on the sill, cats - and keep the tape measure to hand. You will be asked to press a button when something happens, and to read a few distances.

If something goes wrong, every step can be repeated on its own, without redoing the ones already done. You can close whenever you like: nothing is saved until the last screen, and a run already under way ends by itself at the end stop.

path_b.title: What kind of cover is {cover}?
path_b.description:
A profile describes a model of cover: how long it takes to run, how long the slats take to open and how the curtain winds onto the roller. Home Assistant scales it to this cover as soon as it knows what its curtain travel is.

**What you have to do**: pick the profile measured on a cover similar to this one. On the next screen you will measure the curtain travel of this one.

path_c.title: Correct {cover}
path_c.description:
This cover has been given a profile but does not behave as the profile says: the motor may be slower, the curtain heavier, the roller thicker. What you measure here applies to this cover alone and takes precedence over both the profile and the configuration file, if you use one; everything you do not measure goes on coming from the profile.

**What you have to do**: confirm which profile this cover should start from.

refine_scope.title: How far do you want to correct the calibration?
refine_scope.description:
**Cover**: {cover}

**What is about to happen**: one of three things. Three timed runs (two up and one down); those plus three tape readings - the curtain travel, and one at half the travel in each direction; or no timed run at all, four tape readings at a quarter and at three quarters of the travel in each direction and then a check. Each option below says how many movements it costs.

The times alone are enough for a cover whose motor is simply slower or faster than the one the profile was measured on. Add the coefficients when it is wrong *half way* as well: there it is not the motor that turns differently, it is the curtain that winds differently.

The last one is the thorough calibration on its own, for a cover that has been measured already: it keeps every time this cover runs on today and reads nothing but the tape. If its curtain travel has never been measured, that reading comes first and costs no movement of its own: the cover has to be taken to the top for it in any case.

**What you have to do**: choose how far to go. You can always come back and do the rest.

menu_options.times_only: Its own run times only (3 presses, 5 movements)
menu_options.times_and_rolls: Its own times and its own coefficients (3 presses, 3 readings, 8 movements)
menu_options.points_only: Thorough calibration only (no timed run: 4 readings and a check, 10 movements)

home_closed_done.title: Is the cover completely closed?

menu_options.not_right: It did not do what it should

open_brief.title: We are about to measure the ascent
open_brief.description:
![](/myhome_static/ascent_presses.webp)

**Cover**: {cover}

**What is about to happen**: the ascent is measured by two runs, one press each, and this is the first. When you press the button below the cover starts upwards from the base: for the first second or two only the slats open, while the bottom edge stays on its rest, and then the whole curtain begins to rise. The cover is stopped the instant you press, a few centimetres up, and the next screen asks you to look at where it stopped.

**What you have to do**: here you will have to be quick and precise. One press, at the instant the bottom edge leaves the base. You are not timing anything: the instant of the press is the measurement.

The second run comes afterwards, from the base again, and asks for the other press: the instant the cover reaches the end stop at the top and the motor stops, which you recognise by the noise ceasing. The drawing shows both.

The screens that follow carry a single line, because there is no time to read while watching the cover.

Read this at your own pace, get into position, and start the movement yourself when you are ready.

open_lift.title: The cover is opening

menu_options.lifted_off: 1) Press when the bottom edge leaves the base
menu_options.not_right: It did not do what it should

lift_check.title: Where is the bottom edge now?
lift_check.description:
![](/myhome_static/lift_off.webp)

**Cover**: {cover}

**What happened**: the cover was stopped the instant you pressed. Between a press and the motor coming to rest there is always a moment - your own reaction, the command reaching the gateway, the motor braking - and the curtain goes on rising for all of it.

**What you have to do**: look at the bottom edge and say which of the three it is. A few centimetres above the base is what a press that went well looks like. Still resting on the base means the press came before the edge left it: that measurement cannot be repaired, only made again. A hand's breadth or more means the press was late, and a late press is the one case a tape measure can put right.

If in doubt, measure: the reading is the most precise of the three answers, because it puts the instant the edge left the base back where it belongs instead of trusting the press.

menu_options.lift_too_early: It is still touching the base
menu_options.lift_accept: It stands a few centimetres up, go on
menu_options.lift_gap: I want to measure the gap for more precision
menu_options.not_right: It did not do what it should

lift_check_late.title: Where is the bottom edge now?
lift_check_late.description:
![](/myhome_static/lift_off.webp)

**Cover**: {cover}

**What happened**: the cover was stopped the instant you pressed - but the gateway had other commands in its queue and took more than a second to write ours to the bus. The curtain went on rising for all of that, so the gap you are about to see is wider than usual and it is not your doing.

**What you have to do**: look at the bottom edge and say which of the three it is. Still resting on the base means the press came before the edge left it: that measurement cannot be repaired, only made again. Anything above the base is worth measuring here, because on this run the tape is the only thing that can say when the edge really left.

menu_options.lift_too_early: It is still touching the base
menu_options.lift_accept: It stands a few centimetres up, go on
menu_options.lift_gap: I want to measure the gap for more precision
menu_options.not_right: It did not do what it should

lift_gap.title: Measure the gap - {cover}
lift_gap.description:
![](/myhome_static/lift_off.webp)

**What you have to do**: measure from the base - the point where the bottom edge rests when the cover is closed - up to the bottom edge where it is now, and write the centimetres below. That distance says exactly when the edge really left the base, so the slat opening time stops depending on how quick your finger was.

Leaving the field empty goes on without measuring, and the press stands as it was made.

data.gap_cm: Gap between the bottom edge and the base (cm)

data_description.gap_cm: In centimetres, usually between 2 and 5. Decimals may be written with a comma or with a point: 3,5 or 3.5. Leave it empty to go on without measuring.

lift_early.title: The press came too early

menu_options.not_right: It did not do what it should

closed_again.title: Is the cover completely closed again?

menu_options.not_right: It did not do what it should

open_full_brief.title: Now the whole ascent
open_full_brief.description:
![](/myhome_static/top_stop.webp)

**Cover**: {cover}

**What is about to happen**: when you press the button below, the cover starts upwards from the base again and this time it is left to run - the slats open, the whole curtain rises, and at the top the cover stops by itself at its end stop.

**What you have to do**: one press only, at the instant the motor stops at the top. You recognise it by the noise ceasing. Nothing is asked of you at the base this time: that measurement is already made.

The screen during the movement carries a single line, because there is no time to read while watching the cover.

Read this at your own pace, get into position, and start the movement yourself when you are ready.

menu_options.repeat_step: Measure the ascent again from the start

open_top.title: The cover is still rising

menu_options.stopped_open: 2) Press when the motor stops at the top
menu_options.not_right: It did not do what it should

open_result.title: The ascent was measured

open_result_gap.title: The ascent was measured
open_result_gap.description:
**Cover**: {cover}

**What was measured**: slats {slat} s, full ascent {run} s, and a gap of {gap} cm above the base.

The slat opening time above is the one the press produced. The gap you measured replaces it when the values are computed, so what ends up stored may differ from it by a few tenths of a second - that is the whole point of having measured it.

**What you have to do**: if the press at the top and the reading both felt right, go on. Repeating the measurement makes both runs of the ascent again from the base.

close_brief.title: We are about to measure the descent
close_brief.description:
**Cover**: {cover}

**What is about to happen**: when you press the button below, the cover starts downwards from the top and stops by itself once the curtain is down and the slats have closed.

**What you have to do**: here too you will have to be quick and precise, but this time there is only one press, at the instant the motor stops at the bottom.

**Careful**: do not press when the bottom edge touches the base. From there the cover goes on moving for a moment longer, to close the slats. Press only when it stops moving altogether, slats included, that is when the motor stops: you recognise it by the noise ceasing.

A cover comes down a little faster than it goes up, which is why this is measured separately. The screen during the movement carries a single line, because there is no time to read while watching the cover.

Read this at your own pace, get into position, and start the movement yourself when you are ready.

close_bottom.title: The cover is closing
close_bottom.description:
**Cover**: {cover}

Press at the instant the motor stops at the bottom.

menu_options.stopped_closed: Press when the motor stops at the bottom
menu_options.not_right: It did not do what it should

close_result.title: The descent was measured

height.title: What is the curtain travel of {cover}?
height.description:
![](/myhome_static/height.webp)

**What you have to do**: with the cover completely open, measure from the point where the bottom edge of the cover rests when it is closed (the base) up to the bottom edge of the cover in its present position (completely open). In other words, measure the distance the cover travels from fully open to fully closed (or the other way round), and write the centimetres below.

That distance is the curtain travel, and it is the reference every other measurement is compared against. Measure the curtain, not the opening: if the bottom edge rests on a sill rather than on the floor, measure from the sill.

data_description.height: In centimetres. Decimals may be written with a comma or with a point: 198,5 or 198.5.

height_result.title: The curtain travel was written down

menu_options.not_right: It did not do what it should

tape_brief.title: Before the automatic readings

measure_descent.title: Measure {cover} - {percent}% of the way down
measure_descent.description:
![](/myhome_static/reading.webp)

**What happened**: the cover was opened completely and then run down about {percent}% of its travel.

**What you have to do**: measure from the base up to the bottom edge where it is now, and write the centimetres below. The same reference as the curtain travel, so that the two measurements can be compared.

data_description.measured_cm: About {expected} cm is expected; anything within {tolerance} cm of {expected} is perfectly normal. Decimals may be written with a comma or with a point.

measure_ascent.title: Measure {cover} - {percent}% of the way up
measure_ascent.description:
![](/myhome_static/reading.webp)

**What happened**: the cover was closed completely and then run upwards: first the slats opened, then the curtain travelled about {percent}% of its way.

**What you have to do**: measure from the base up to the bottom edge where it is now, and write the centimetres below. A cover is not loaded the same way going up and going down, which is why the same fraction is measured twice.

data_description.measured_cm: About {expected} cm is expected; anything within {tolerance} cm of {expected} is perfectly normal. Decimals may be written with a comma or with a point.

measure_verify.title: Check {cover} - {percent}% of the way down
measure_verify.description:
![](/myhome_static/reading.webp)

**What happened**: the cover was taken to a position nothing was measured at, so this is a real check and not a repetition.

**What you have to do**: measure the height of the bottom edge one last time, from the same reference as before, and write the centimetres below. The next screen shows the difference between the measured position and the position estimated by Home Assistant.

data_description.measured_cm: About {expected} cm is expected; anything within {tolerance} cm of {expected} is perfectly normal. Decimals may be written with a comma or with a point.

tape_result.title: The reading was written down
tape_result.description:
**Cover**: {cover} - read at {percent}% of the travel

**What was written down**: {measured} cm from the base to the bottom edge.

**What you have to do**: if that is the number you read off the tape, go on. If you suspect you measured from the wrong point, repeat the measurement: the cover goes back to its end stop and runs the same distance again, so the reading can be taken under the same conditions. If the cover did not do what it should (it never moved, or it moved the wrong way), say so below: it is stopped and the movements of this step are made again.

menu_options.tape_not_right: It did not do what it should

verify_offer.title: Do you want to check the cover?

verify_result.title: Where the cover really stopped
verify_result.description:
**Cover**: {cover} - **gap**: {deviation} cm

That is the distance between where the cover really stopped and where Home Assistant believed it would. One or two centimetres are normal and already a very good approximation; three or more mean that this cover does not behave like the profile assigned to it.

**What you have to do**: go on, or repeat the measurement if you think the reading was wrong. If available, the correction measures this cover separately.

menu_options.path_c: Correct this cover with its own measurements

profile_name.title: Name this kind of cover
profile_name.description:
{cover} has been measured, and what was measured describes every cover similar to it. Give that kind a name and the others will be calibrated in two screens instead of ten.

**What you have to do**: write a short name - letters, digits and underscores only, no spaces and no accents, because it is also a key of the configuration file. Something like `tall`, `bedrooms` or `kitchen_door`.

The name is asked for now because it appears in the summary on the next screen. A name already in use is not refused: the profile of that name is **replaced** by the one just measured, and that is how a cover whose first measurement went badly is measured again. A `cover_profiles:` block of the same name in the configuration file is left untouched and has lower priority than the measured profile.

summary_basic.title: What was measured

menu_options.refine: Continue with the thorough calibration (~2 minutes, 5 more readings)

summary_short.title: What was measured

summary_correction.title: What was measured

menu_options.refine: Continue with the thorough calibration (~2 minutes, 5 more readings)

summary_precise.title: What was measured

saved.title: Calibration saved
saved.description:
Done: the calibration of {cover} is saved. It is applied when this dialog is closed, and from then on {cover} moves on the values measured on it just now. The entity's attributes then say `guided` under “Calibration source” — that is, **{origin}** — and carry the numbers themselves under “Opening time”, “Closing time”, “Slat time”, the roll coefficients and “Height”.

**Where to find it again**: here under Configure → Calibrations, and the profile “{profile}”, measured on this cover, under Configure → Profiles and covers. If one day you want the values written in the configuration file back, all you have to do is delete the calibration from that screen.

**What you can do now**: calibrate another cover, or close. Every cover similar to this one takes two screens, by choosing “(B) It is similar to a cover already measured”.

saved_profile.title: Calibration saved
saved_profile.description:
Done: {cover} now follows the profile “{profile}”, and does so from the moment this dialog is closed. No run of its own was timed here: the only thing measured on this cover is its curtain travel, and the profile's times are scaled to it. The entity's attributes then say `profile {profile}` under “Calibration source” — that is, **{origin}** — and the numbers themselves are under “Opening time”, “Closing time”, “Slat time”, the roll coefficients and “Height”.

**Where to find it again**: here under Configure → Calibrations, and the profile “{profile}” under Configure → Profiles and covers, where it is shared with every cover that follows it. If one day you want the values written in the configuration file back, all you have to do is delete the calibration from that screen.

**What you can do now**: give the same profile to another cover, or close. If {cover} turns out to stop in the wrong place, “(C) It has a profile but stops in the wrong place” measures its own run times.

saved_refined.title: Calibration saved
saved_refined.description:
Done: the calibration of {cover} is saved, and it is applied when this dialog is closed. {cover} goes on following the profile “{profile}”, and what was just measured on this cover alone now takes precedence over it; everything that was not measured here still comes from the profile. The entity's attributes then say `{source}` under “Calibration source” — that is, **{origin}** — and the numbers themselves are under “Opening time”, “Closing time”, “Slat time”, the roll coefficients and “Height”.

**Where to find it again**: here under Configure → Calibrations, where you can look at the values again, correct them by hand or delete them. The profile itself was not touched: the other covers that follow it are unaffected.

**What you can do now**: calibrate another cover, or close.

cancelled.title: Calibration cancelled
cancelled.description:
Nothing was saved: {cover} is no longer being calibrated and answers ordinary commands again, exactly as before.

**If it was still moving**, it is not stopped: a run started by the calibration has no end of its own and carries on to the end stop it was heading for.

expired.title: The session expired through inactivity
expired.description:
The calibration session was inactive for too long, so {cover} is no longer being calibrated and responds to normal commands again.

**Nothing was saved**: the measurements taken so far were discarded, and getting them back means starting again from the beginning. If {cover} was still moving, it was asked to stop where it was.

A screen with a progress bar has no Cancel button of its own: the way out of one is to close the dialog, which gives the cover back straight away.

refused_unknown_cover.title: That cover is not there any more
refused_unknown_cover.description:
The cover is no longer part of this gateway's configuration, so there is nothing to measure. Nothing was saved.

If you renamed or moved it in the configuration file, reload the integration and try again.

refused_already_calibrating.title: This cover is already being calibrated
refused_already_calibrating.description:
There is another dialog open on this cover, or the `cover_calibration_run` service is driving it. Two calibrations on the same motor would each measure a run the other one stopped, so this one was not started.

**What you have to do**: finish or close the other one, then try again.

problem_no_echo.title: The cover did not answer
problem_no_echo.description:
**Cover**: {cover}

The command reached the bus but the actuator never reported that it had started moving, so there is no instant to measure against and the step was abandoned.

**The cover may still be moving**: the command really did go out, so the motor most likely started. A stop was sent straight after the failure, but if the cover is still running, stop it yourself before repeating the step.

**What you have to do**: check that the cover is not jammed, and repeat the step. If it happens every time, this actuator does not report its own state and the guided calibration cannot measure it.

problem_not_delivered.title: The command never reached the bus
problem_not_delivered.description:
The gateway never wrote our command to the bus - it would not take it, it dropped it, or it never said what became of it - so {cover} was never asked to move and nothing was measured.

**What you have to do**: check that the gateway is connected - the integration page says so - and repeat the step.

problem_not_stopped.title: The cover could not be stopped

problem_busy.title: The cover is already moving

problem_bad_point.title: Those two presses cannot both be right
problem_bad_point.description:
The recorded times are inconsistent: the cover cannot have stopped before it started, nor opened its slats after arriving.

**What you have to do**: repeat the step and press once for each event, at the moment it happens.

problem_timeout.title: Nothing was pressed in time
problem_timeout.description:
This screen waits about a minute and a half for the press it is about, and nothing was pressed in that time. There is no instant left to measure from, so the step was abandoned rather than timed from a press that came afterwards.

**What you have to do**: repeat the step and this time press as soon as the cover does what the screen describes.

gateway.name: Gateway

cover_calibration_run.name: Calibrate cover (run)
cover_calibration_run.description: Sends the cover to one end, then runs it for exactly the motor time a set_cover_position 50 would use with its current configuration and stops it there, so the height of the bar can be measured for cover_calibration_compute.

direction.name: Direction
direction.description: Which run to measure: 'close' starts from fully open and runs half the curtain time, 'open' starts from fully closed and runs the slat opening time plus half the curtain time.

cover_calibration_compute.name: Calibrate cover (compute)
cover_calibration_compute.description: Turns the heights measured after cover_calibration_run into the roll of this cover - one per direction when both runs were measured - and returns a cover_profiles snippet ready to paste into myhome.yaml.

height.name: Curtain travel
height.description: Distance in centimetres between the fully open and the fully closed bar (the travel, not the opening).

closed_half_cm.name: Height after the closing half run
closed_half_cm.description: Centimetres between the floor and the bottom of the bar, measured after cover_calibration_run with direction 'close'.

opened_half_cm.name: Height after the opening half run
opened_half_cm.description: The same measurement after direction 'open'. Optional: it is what gives the separate opening_roll, and without it only the closing roll is worked out.

slat_time.name: Slat opening time
slat_time.description: Seconds of slat-only travel. It is an input, never an answer: given here it is used as it stands, otherwise the value configured on the cover is.

closed_run_seconds.name: Closing run length
closed_run_seconds.description: Motor seconds the closing run really lasted, as reported by cover_calibration_run. Only needed when the cover's times changed in between: it defaults to the same value the run computed.

opened_run_seconds.name: Opening run length
opened_run_seconds.description: Motor seconds the opening run really lasted, as reported by cover_calibration_run. Only needed when the cover's times changed in between: it defaults to the same value the run computed.
